items.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: I played with him back in the 50s. ... Well I first played with him and back then we did some recording for Grand Award, the Command label with Pee Wee Irwin.

ctx.x: I think it’s a good opinion.

I’m surmising this myself on my own, I don’t know whether I’m right or wrong. I think it is. I’ve thought about it and I think it’s sad. Because like you say I just don’t see too many black players playing this style of music. I can’t think of any. I mean I see some of the old timers that are still around like Joe Wilder and Jackie Williams, of course Milt Hinton just passed away but he was part of it. I played with him back in the 50s. But I wish there were more. John Lamb I played with here with Buster Cooper…
Well I think it was well said, your thoughts anyway. Everyone has particular memories of Milt Hinton. Do you have any specific things?
